affordance_in_statement: The network topology guarantees that a message broadcast from any location will reach every other location without ever encountering a closed loop.
removal_suggestion: Do not guarantee connectedness and acyclicity; instead allow the m = n − 1 connections to form a general graph and define the required minimum-cost primary-connecting subgraph accordingly. This removes the unique-tree-subgraph shortcut, though it changes the computational nature of the task.

common_affordance: The connections form a connected acyclic graph, hence a tree; therefore the answer is the unique minimal subtree containing all primary locations.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It applies a Kruskal/union-find minimum-spanning-tree strategy by sorting all edges, rather than selecting only the tree edges on paths needed to connect primary locations; this can include irrelevant branches.

recommended_edit: Replace the explicit no-closed-loop topology guarantee with a general-graph topology in the scenario, while retaining the same primary-connectivity objective; otherwise there is no wording-only edit that defeats the surviving tree-based solutions without changing the core problem.
regression_risk: Allowing general graphs could make the existing MST-style approach appear more plausible, but it still does not solve the general minimum Steiner tree problem.
